jobs.title: AI Deployment Engineer

security, data governance, and customer satisfaction standards. **Accountabilities** Deployment \& Implementation * Design, build, and deploy AI\-powered solutions using the Hatz AI platform as the primary solution * Assess customer data sources and requirements to determine solution architecture, and establish secure, compliant data pipelines connecting customer systems to AI workflows * Serve as the active deployment resource for customer AI requests, executing technical implementations of AI Agents, Workflows, and Applications in production environments Multi\-Platform AI Expertise * investments * Evaluate requests across all three platforms to recommend the best solution architecture, including when to migrate workloads between platforms Data Management \& Governance * Evaluate customer data sources for quality, completeness, and AI suitability, and work with customers to remediate issues affecting solution performance * Design data validation, cleansing, and preparation workflows, and establish architecture patterns that separate, secure, and govern customer data across Hatz, Co\-Pilot, and Claude * Document data source specifications, transformation logic, and constraints that may impact feasibility * Determine whether Co\-Pilot or Claude issues warrant standard support or vendor escalation Strategic Assessment \& Growth * Identify requests that warrant advanced prompt engineering techniques optimized for Hatz AI, Co\-Pilot, and Claude, and understand each platform's strengths, limitations, and use case alignment * Champion AI security and data governance standards across all deployments * Document solutions, configurations, and lessons learned to build organizational knowledge, and stay current with AI/ML developments, platform updates, and industry best practices Collaboration * Work closely with the AI \& Development Director to align deployments with internal development roadmaps and data architecture standards * Coordinate with governance considerations * Experience with customer data sources and data quality challenges; familiarity with ETL/ELT processes or API\-based data connections * Familiarity with ticketing and service management systems (HaloPSA experience a plus) * Excellent technical communication skills with both technical and non\-technical audiences * Self\-directed problem\-solving ability and comfort working in a fast\-paced, growing team * Working knowledge of, or ability to quickly learn, multiple AI platforms and their tools **Preferred Qualifications** * Prior experience with Hatz AI platform or similar AI\-as\-a\-service solutions * Hands\-on experience with Microsoft Co\-Pilot, Azure OpenAI, or Anthropic Claude API/platform integrations * Background in customer\-facing technical support, professional services, project management, or service delivery * Experience defining support processes and categorization systems in managed services or MSP environments * Experience with data quality assessment, validation, or master data management; familiarity with GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, or similar compliance frameworks * Background in data architecture or database administration **Core Competencies** * Multi\-Platform Technical Proficiency: Hatz AI mastery (primary), Co\-Pilot and Claude ecosystem knowledge, prompt engineering, solution architecture, platform selection * Data Stewardship: Data quality assessment, governance mindset, attention to data accuracy and security * Customer Focus: Active listening, responsiveness, solution orientation, ability to translate data jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer, Customer Agents
jobs.description: **About Attuned Intelligence** ------------------------------ Attuned Intelligence is automating patient access for community health centers and health systems. We build AI\-powered voice agents that automate how patients enter, navigate, and stay connected to care — from the first phone call to a scheduled visit. Every missed call at a health center is a missed appointment. Every language barrier is a gap in care. We exist to close those gaps. Our platform handles hundreds of thousands of calls per month across multiple languages, routing patients to the right care team on the first try — and integrating directly with Epic to automate scheduling, appointment management, and clinical workflows. We're a fast\-moving team backed by a deep understanding of agentic systems and healthcare operations with a mission\-driven approach to building technology that makes care more accessible and equitable. **The role** ------------ We're looking for a hands\-on AI solutions engineer to build and improve agents for our healthcare customers. You'll translate requirements gathered by the Customer Delivery team into reliable agent capabilities, developing prompts, conversation flows, and tool integrations that improve patient access and reduce administrative work. Partnering with platform engineers, you'll prototype new capabilities, test the complete experience, and turn recurring customer needs into reusable solutions across the Attuned platform. Success means customers have reliable agents, know how to use them effectively, and can see measurable improvements in their operations. **What you'll do** ------------------ * **Build and validate customer solutions.** Design prompts, conversation flows, knowledge content, and tool integrations. Test complete experiences against realistic scenarios and customer expectations. * **Develop new agent capabilities.** Translate customer problems into new agent behaviors, tools, and workflows. Prototype and validate solutions, building directly where appropriate and partnering with platform engineers on capabilities that require product or infrastructure changes. * **Test and troubleshoot systematically.** Develop scalable testing systems that can run representative customer scenarios. Reproduce failures, distinguish prompt and configuration issues from model or platform problems, and verify that changes improve the intended behavior. * **Drive ongoing customer outcomes.** Use call results and feedback gathered by Customer Delivery to recommend and implement agent improvements and identify opportunities to expand the agent's usefulness. Measure progress through successful task completion, patient experience, and reduced staff effort while preserving privacy and appropriate human handoffs. * **Turn customer learning into product improvements.** Identify needs shared across customers and contribute reusable capabilities, implementation approaches, and recommendations for the product roadmap. **What you'll bring** --------------------- * 3\-5 years experience with hands\-on experience building LLM\-based agents, conversational experiences, or workflow automations, with concrete examples of what you built and how you tested it. * Experience with voice AI, conversation design, speech recognition, or text\-to\-speech systems. * Strong writing and structured reasoning: you can turn an ambiguous request into clear instructions, decision logic, and observable success criteria. * Practical programming or scripting ability, plus comfort working with APIs, JSON, version control, and logs to build and debug workflows. * A methodical approach to troubleshooting. You investigate what happened, reproduce the problem, and validate the fix against the actual user experience. * Clear communication with technical and nontechnical teammates, including explaining dependencies and surfacing missing requirements early. **Helpful experience** ---------------------- * Agent tool calling, evaluation frameworks, or automated scenario testing. * Customer implementations, technical support, or another role that translates real\-world operating requirements into working software.

jobs.title: Application Developer, Automation & AI Engineer
jobs.description: The Application Developer, Automation \& AI will join the Corporate Technology team to build, deploy, and support internal web applications and AI\-assisted automations that allow employees to work more efficiently and effectively. This is a hands\-on role that splits time between two areas. The first is developing new applications and automations in Node.js, Python, and Go. The second is serving as a support resource for AI\-built applications created by colleagues across the firm, helping them debug, review, and ship their work onto the firm's internal infrastructure. The ideal candidate is a practical developer with a solid IT foundation, including a working understanding of networking and DNS. We are looking for a proactive candidate who is ready to join a fast\-paced environment, is eager to learn, and wants to help shape coding standards for the firm. This position is based in the firm's Richmond, VA headquarters, and reports to the Chief Technology Officer. Responsibilities and job duties: * Design, Build and maintain internal web applications, APIS, and workflow automations. * Server as a first point of contact for employees with coding questions: troubleshooting errors, reviewing code (Including AI\-generated code), and guiding colleagues through version control and development * Help colleagues move prototypes built on outside platforms onto the firm's internal hosting environment * Deploy and support applications on the firm's containerized platform (Kubernetes with Git\-based deployments) using established templates, in partnership with the infrastructure team * Build integrations with internal and third\-party systems through REST APIs * Maintain existing internal applications and help modernize them over time * Use AI\-assisted development tools to speed up delivery while making sure the resulting code is secure, tested, and maintainable * Write clear documentation and help establish development standards, templates, and best practices as the team grows Professional skills \& Experience: * 2\+ years of development experience in Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js), whether professional, through internships, or through substantial academic or personal projects * Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases (MariaDB/MySQL or PostgreSQL) * Proficiency with Git and collaborative workflows (branching, pull requests, code review) * Foundational IT knowledge, including networking, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS and TLS certificates, and the Linux command line * Hands\-on experience with AI coding assistants (e.g., Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Claude) and the judgment to review and correct their output * Strong troubleshooting skills and the patience to explain technical issues to non\-technical colleagues Preferred experience includes: * Go * Containers (Docker or Podman), with exposure to Kubernetes, Helm or GitOps tools. * CI/CD pipelines (Github Actions) * Modern web frameworks such as FastAPI, Express, Next.js, or React * PowerShell, bash and python scripting Candidates must submit a resume to be considered for this position. The final salary or hourly rate offered for this role will fall within the range set below based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, geographic location, experience, skills, and competencies. Base Compensation: $$85,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 Annually

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer II
jobs.description: : **About Us** ------------ LiquidXR is an expanding, well\-funded, early\-stage company building a platform to digitize human movement. We are creating next\-gen wearables using proprietary MetalGel sensor technology, capturing and feeding movement data to our machine learning\-enhanced algorithms and SDKs, which connect to any modern computer or development environment. We are partnered with several high\-quality companies co\-developing products using our tech, and we are advancing our platform to enable all types of body movement data capture and analysis across multiple areas of use (sports performance, wellness, robotics/AI, clinical/healthcare, and gaming/XR). Our tight knit hardware and software team is comprised of experts in product and UX development, biomechanics, algorithms and machine learning, software platform and experience development, electronic engineering, and soft goods industrial design. Individually and collectively, this is a team who gets things done and among us, countless products have been launched worldwide. We are passionate about creating a transformative platform and we are fortunate to work on cool products using our tech along the way. **The Role** ------------ We are seeking a skilled and motivated **Electrical Engineer II** to design and iterate on the electronics behind our wearable platform. In this role, you will contribute to the electrical architecture of our platform hardware and products, from initial concept to mass production. You will be responsible for designing, prototyping, bringing up, and validating low\-power sensing electronics and flexible interconnect systems, with a special focus on compact, robust solutions for body\-worn devices. This is a hands\-on role for an engineer who is comfortable at the bench with a scope in one hand and a soldering iron in the other. : **What You'll Do** ------------------ * **Drive Electrical Design:** Contribute to the end\-to\-end electrical design and PCB development for wearable platform components, low\-power sensor interfaces, and wearable consumer electronics. * **Schematic \& PCB factors. * **Validate Products \& System Integration:** Develop and execute test plans to validate electrical systems, battery management, power regulation, and sensor interface circuits against internal and external requirements. * **Bring Up and Debug:** Build, bring up, and characterize prototype hardware; diagnose issues at the board and system level using scopes, logic analyzers, and lab instrumentation. * **Produce Technical Documentation:** Develop and maintain meticulous engineering documentation, including schematics, layout files, bills of materials (BOMs), test plans, and test reports. * **Troubleshoot \& Optimize:** Apply structured problem\-solving, EMI/EMC compliance techniques, and root\-cause failure analysis to diagnose and resolve electrical bugs and signal integrity issues. * **Keep Work Moving:** Manage your own deliverables across multiple concurrent programs, hit committed dates, and flag risks early. * **Collaborate and Integrate:** Work closely with product management, mechanical engineers, manufacturing technicians, firmware and software engineers, and soft goods industrial designers, as well as external partners, to ensure seamless product integration and cohesive final products. * **Support Production Scaling:** Assist with design for manufacturability and test (DFM/DFT) and work alongside manufacturing partners as designs move toward volume production. : **What You'll Bring (Qualifications)** -------------------------------------- * **Education:** Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field. * **Experience:** 5\+ years of hands\-on electrical engineering experience designing, bringing up, and debugging complex PCBA hardware (preferably in consumer electronics, wearables, flexible electronics, or IoT devices). * **CAD Tools:** Strong proficiency in ECAD design software (e.g., Altium Designer, Eagle, or KiCad) for schematic capture and PCB layout. * **Hardware Domain Knowledge:** Experience with low\-power microcontrollers (e.g., ARM Cortex\-M), wireless protocols (BLE, Wi\-Fi), power management (PMICs, battery charging), and analog sensor signal conditioning. * **Lab Debugging:** Proficiency with standard EE lab equipment (oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, multimeters, soldering stations). * **Standards \& DFM:** Understanding of IPC standards for PCB design, DFM/DFT principles, and design for EMI/EMC compliance. **Who You Are** --------------- * **An Owner:** You possess a powerful ownership mindset and take full accountability for your projects from concept to completion. * **A Proactive Driver:** You are a self\-starter who can "catch the vision and run with it." You thrive with autonomy and are skilled at moving projects forward with minimal oversight. * **Coachable and Curious:** You actively seek feedback from senior engineers, ask good questions, and apply what you learn quickly. * **A Team Player:** You are a natural collaborator who communicates clearly and works effectively with cross\-functional teams to achieve shared goals. * **Adaptable and Resilient:** You excel at managing multiple priorities without sacrificing quality. You see the challenges of a startup environment as opportunities. * **Detail\-Oriented:** You have a keen eye for detail and are committed to producing high\-quality, well\-documented work. **Compensation, Benefits, Hours** --------------------------------- This is a full\-time employee position in Los Angeles, CA. You will be provided health care benefits (currently, gold PPO coverage with Blue Shield, as well as dental and vision) starting within 30 days of employment. We are an open PTO company. This is primarily an in\-person role in our Los Angeles office which houses our R\&D and prototype manufacturing and testing equipment. Some remote work will be reasonable. Occasional travel may be required domestically and internationally. **DISCLAIMER** -------------- We are an affirmative action, equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Lead Edge Engineer
jobs.description: **About Us** Queue builds robots to fill prescriptions. Our machine is designed to take stock bottles of medication and produce counted, labeled vials, so that pharmacists and technicians can spend their time on patients. Our first product is built to work behind the pharmacy counter and to be operated by pharmacy staff. **About the Role** We are building out the Edge squad: the engineers who write the software that runs on our machine and tells its hardware what to do. You are a hands\-on technical lead. You own the edge software end to end, from design and code to release and behavior in the field, and you raise the bar for everyone who builds it. You build to one rule and hold the squad to it: when the machine cannot confirm a step, it stops safely and says why. This is a lead\-level role: a staff engineer's technical bar, plus delivery through a team. It is hands\-on, and it is not a people\-management role. **What You'll Own** * **Design and code** — The design of the edge software and the code that carries it, from the links to the boards to the state machines that sequence each fill. You stay in the code and review the squad's. * **Contracts at the boundaries** — The contracts with the microcontrollers and the vision service. You design and version them so that old and new versions work together through a release. * **Releases and field behavior** — How a release of the edge software is built, tested and shipped, what the software reports from the field, and how it is diagnosed from a distance. You work on updates with the platform and systems reliability engineers, and on the image with the engineers who own it. * **The seams** — Where the edge software meets firmware, vision, the cloud and the image. A fault that falls between two squads is yours until it is fixed, and you fix it with the squad on the other side. * **The squad's bar** — What you accept in review becomes the standard, so you define it crisply, hold it every time and measure quality against it. You grow the engineers around you into leaders: you pair and coach, give them the lead and back them, and you interview the ones who join. * **Decisions in writing** — You write decisions down with the options you weighed and why, and share them early for challenge across the squads, so engineers can make the next decision without you. * **Fail\-closed behavior** — The rule on every path the squad owns: when the machine cannot confirm a step, it stops safely and says why. You design the failure path first, and the squad does too. What stays with others, so that you know where your work stops: the operating\-system image stays with the engineers who own it, the cloud with the platform engineers, and the call that a release is ready with software leadership. **First 90 Days** * **Day 30:** You have built the edge software, run it on a bench and merged changes through review. With the firmware, vision and platform engineers, you have traced a fill across every seam, and you can name each point where it has to stop if a step cannot be confirmed. * **Day 60:** You own one seam end to end with the squad on the other side: its code, its contract and what the edge software does when the other side fails. You have planned the squad's next release with its engineers, each change with an owner, and written down the bar you hold in review. * **Day 90:** You have scoped and reviewed a change that an engineer on the squad has taken through release to machines on the bench, with its failure paths tested first. You have written down the reasons behind one design decision, so that engineers can act on it without you, and the squad reviews to what you wrote down. **What We're Looking For** *Must\-Have* * Ownership — you have written production C, C\+\+ or Rust on Linux and owned a device's software end to end, from the first design to the fault found in the field, including faults that started in another team's part of the system. * Hardware integration over buses — CAN, RS\-485 and other serial links, USB. You debug at the wire when the logs and the hardware disagree. * Real\-time orchestration and state machines — you have designed the sequencing of motion, sensing and I/O where partial failure is normal, and you design the failure path first: when a step cannot be confirmed, the system stops safely and says why. * MCU boundary literacy — you understand how a microcontroller runs and what it exposes to a Linux host, and you have designed versioned device protocols with firmware that held up through change, for example a protobuf schema, a CAN message set or a register map. * Embedded Linux integration — you have done substantial work getting software running well on an embedded Linux system: its services, devices, start\-up, configuration and updates, worked out with the owners of its image. * Connected device fleets — you have run devices in the field: updates, remote diagnostics, telemetry, and the recovery of a unit you cannot touch. * Hardened device platforms — you have shipped software on devices with verified start\-up, signed updates and a read\-only system, and you design software that works within them. * Technical leadership — you have made a team's engineering better through design, review and mentoring, without needing a title. You ask for challenge on your own designs, change course when the evidence says so, and say early, with data, when a commitment will slip. When several things go wrong at once, you put them in order and finish one before you start the next. The edge software is written in Rust, and you will work in it every day. Rust in production is strongly preferred. *Nice\-to\-Have* * Industrial x86 and ARM platforms in a shipped product. * Full ownership of an embedded Linux distribution: building and maintaining the image of a shipped device, from what goes into it to how it updates. * Kernel and board bring\-up: drivers, device trees and boot on a new board. * NVIDIA Jetson: JetPack and Linux for Tegra, secure boot, field updates and the inference stack. * Robotics, medical devices, automotive or industrial automation. **How We Hire** * **Recruiter Screen** (30 min) * **Technical Interview** (90 min) — a take\-home exercise of 2 to 3 hours, in C, C\+\+ or Rust, sent at least 24 hours before: a small piece of device software built around a state machine, which has to stay correct when power is lost at any step. We go through it together, then build on it. * **Design Interview** (60 min) — the path a new version of the software takes to a fleet of machines, with the failure cases in from the start, and where the edge software's decisions stop and another squad's begin. * **Leadership Interview** (60 min) — how you lead through a team. Two interviewers score each technical stage independently. **What We Offer** * Ownership — the edge software end to end, from design to the field * Hard problems: real\-time sequencing across boards, the seams with firmware, vision and the cloud, and machines in the field you cannot touch * Small team, zero bureaucracy, high trust **Why Join Us Now?** *Impact \& Growth* * **Direct Impact:** Your design decisions are the ones every change to the edge software builds on * **Growth:** The work runs from one change on the bench to how the software behaves on every machine in the field *Team and Culture* * Reports to the Head of Software Engineering with significant autonomy and influence * **Who You Work With:** You work every day with the engineers who build the edge software, and with the firmware, vision, platform and systems reliability squads at its seams * **Where We Work:** On site at our headquarters in the Bay Area; this work needs the hardware in front of you **Our Values** * **Servant Leadership** * **Do the Hard Things** * **Own Your Work** * **Default is Now** Servant Leadership comes first in this role: you make the engineers around you better, and the squads you depend on more successful. **Contact: If you have any questions, please contact us at** **careers@queue.inc**

jobs.title: Marketing Web Developer (Front End)
jobs.description: Atticor is an AI\-powered legal services platform redefining how lawyers deliver justice to injured people. Great lawyers serve their clients best when they can focus on legal practice, not on troubleshooting their case management system, tracking medical records, dealing with accounting headaches, or managing marketing campaigns. Atticor handles the complex machinery of the modern legal business, liberating top\-tier lawyers to do what they do best: practice law. Atticor was built by legal entrepreneurs who revolutionized mass claims litigation at scale and built technology and operational infrastructure that has served over 1\.5 million clients and generated over $3 billion in gross recoveries, comprising a Case Acquisition Engine, Decision Infrastructure, Agentic AI Workflow \& Operations, and an Institutional\-Grade Backbone. **About the role** Atticor Group LLC is hiring a **Marketing Web Developer** to **build the landing pages and websites** that drive client acquisition across a portfolio of national legal brands. This is a **front end** **role** first. You will own how our pages look, load, and convert. You will sit **inside the marketing team**, not an engineering org. Your work ships fast, gets tested against live paid traffic, and is measured by conversion rate and cost per signed case. If you love pixel\-level craft and also care whether the page actually performs, this is the job. Full stack skills are welcome, but we are hiring for front end excellence. A great candidate is the person a designer and a media buyer both want on their project. This is a **full\-time, remote** role reporting to our Director of Marketing. Compensation for the position includes an annual base salary of $140,000 to $160,000, commensurate with experience, plus the role is eligible for a year\-end discretionary bonus and benefits. **What** **you'll** **do** * **Build landing pages at volume.** Design and develop high\-converting campaign pages in Unbounce and custom HTML/CSS/JS, often several per week across multiple brands and case types. * **Build and maintain brand websites.** Develop new pages, templates, and features on WordPress (custom themes). * **Ship A/B tests.** Build page variants, partner with media buyers on hypotheses, and iterate based on results. * **Protect performance.** Hit Core Web Vitals targets on mobile, where most of our traffic lands. Optimize images, scripts, fonts, and third\-party tags. * **Implement tracking correctly.** Work in Google Tag Manager, fire pixel and server\-side conversion events, and preserve attribution parameters (UTMs, click IDs) through every form submit. * **Translate design into code.** Turn Figma files, mockups, and rough briefs into polished, responsive, accessible pages without hand\-holding. * **Build reusable systems.** Create templates, component libraries, and build standards so the next page ships faster than the last. * **Use AI tooling to move faster.** Use tools like Claude Code to accelerate builds while holding a high bar for the code that ships. **What you bring** * 4\+ years building production websites and landing pages, with a portfolio of live work we can click through * Expert HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript proficiency: You can build a polished, responsive page from scratch without a framework * Strong visual eye. You notice spacing, type, and hierarchy problems before a designer points them out * Hands\-on experience with a landing page platform (Unbounce, Instapage, Webflow, or similar) and its limits * WordPress theme development experience (PHP templates, custom fields, hooks) * Mobile\-first mindset and a track record of fast pages (Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals) * Working knowledge of Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, Google Ads conversion tracking, and GA4 * Experience building and debugging forms: validation, hidden fields, spam prevention, and third\-party integrations * Conversion rate optimization experience: you have run A/B tests and can talk about what won and why * Comfort with Git and a basic deploy workflow * Speed and judgment. You can turn a brief into a live page in a day or two and know which details matter * Clear communication with non\-technical partners: media buyers, designers, attorneys, and intake teams **Nice to have** * Full stack experience: Node.js, Next.js or React, REST APIs, SQL, Supabase or similar * Server\-side tracking (Meta Conversions API, Google enhanced conversions, server\-side GTM) * Background in legal, healthcare, financial services, or another regulated, lead\-gen\-heavy industry * Figma or design skills strong enough to produce a page without a designer **What success looks like** **First 30 days.** You have shipped your first live landing pages, learned our build standards and tracking setup, and can launch a standard campaign page without help. **First 60 days.** You own the landing page queue. Media buyers come to you directly, pages go live on schedule, and tracking fires correctly the first time. **First 90 days.** You have improved the system itself: faster templates, better mobile performance, and at least one A/B test win that measurably lifted conversion rate. Atticor Group LLC is an equal opportunity employer. Atticor is an Equal Opportunity Employer. For California residents, you will receive our CCPA information on your application confirmation page.

jobs.title: Quality Systems and Manufacturing Excellence Lead
jobs.description: **Quality Systems and Manufacturing Excellence Lead** ===================================================== **Barbco, Inc. — East Canton, Ohio** **Build what quality looks like at Barbco** ------------------------------------------- It’s 8:07 a.m. in East Canton. You’ve just walked the floor, spotted a potential fit\-up risk in welding, and paused the job to prevent a downstream rework. By 9:30, you’re with Engineering refining a practical inspection plan for a new equipment platform. After lunch, you’re reviewing supplier nonconformance trends with Purchasing and preparing clear, visual standards that the assembly team can use tomorrow. This is how you move quality upstream—every day. ### **About Barbco** Barbco, Inc. is a family\-owned American manufacturer with decades of experience designing and building underground construction equipment for the trenchless industry. We’re growing, expanding product lines, upgrading manufacturing systems, and investing in our people to power the company’s next generation. ### **Your mandate** This is not an ISO certification\-driven position. Your mission is to architect, implement, and continuously improve a practical, sustainable Barbco quality system that works on the floor, improves products, strengthens accountability, reduces rework, and serves customers better. You will report to senior management and have the visibility and support to drive meaningful, company\-wide impact. ### **What you will lead** * Design, deploy, and iterate Barbco’s internal quality management system focused on real\-world use. * Define inspection processes, quality gates, documentation, and standards across manufacturing with clear accountability. * Drive root\-cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions; lead continuous improvement initiatives. * Own nonconforming material control, product holds, rework, corrective actions, and final disposition. * Improve incoming, in\-process, final inspection, and product\-release processes; create measurable metrics and report trends. * Investigate quality issues from customers, warranty, suppliers, and internal manufacturing; communicate findings and actions. * Elevate supplier quality and incoming\-material expectations in partnership with Purchasing. * Support welding, fabrication, machining, assembly, hydraulic, electrical, and finished\-equipment quality. * Ensure drawings, specifications, work instructions, inspection criteria, and engineering changes are understood and followed. * Build practical documentation employees can actually use; train and coach teams in problem solving. * Champion a culture where quality belongs to everyone; exercise the authority to stop a process when warranted. * Enable new\-product introduction and Barbco’s expansion into new equipment and markets. ### **Where you’ll plug in** Work closely with Production, Engineering, Operations, Purchasing, Dealer Support, and senior management to identify problems early and prevent defects from moving downstream. ### **What makes you successful** * Hands\-on manufacturing quality leadership experience with a track record of building or materially improving a quality system. * Deep skill in root\-cause analysis and corrective action. * Ability to read and interpret drawings, specifications, tolerances, and inspection requirements. * Knowledge of measurement, inspection, calibration, and shop\-floor quality processes. * Comfort collaborating directly with production employees, supervisors, engineers, suppliers, and customers. * Strong organization and documentation habits; sound judgment to make tough quality calls. * Change leadership that aligns quality and production as one team. * Action\-oriented, practical problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset. * Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, 8D, FMEA, CAPA, APQP, and supplier quality is valuable—results matter more than acronyms. * Four\-year degree helpful but not required; significant manufacturing experience, technical education, quality credentials, and proven leadership all count. ### **Why Barbco** * Direct access to leadership; your work won’t disappear into a large corporate department. * See results quickly in collaboration with engineers, craftsmen, dealers, and customers. * We’re investing in new products and equipment platforms, manufacturing capabilities, technology and business systems, training and employee development, dealer and customer support, continuous improvement, and the next generation of Barbco. At Barbco, quality is how we design it, build it, document it, improve it, and stand behind it. For the right person, this role offers significant opportunity to grow with the company and shape our quality future. ### **The person we’re looking for** You can walk onto the shop floor, understand what’s happening, ask the right questions, help solve the issue, and then put a system in place so we don’t solve the same problem twice. You’re firm without being adversarial, and you know production and quality are on the same team. Most of all, you want to build—not just maintain. ### **Market signal** Industry research underscores the importance of QMS ownership, CAPA/root\-cause leadership, audit capability, technical drawing and fabrication literacy, and the ability to influence production. ### **Proficiencies** * Quality Inspection Experience * Continuous Improvement * 5 Why (Root Cause Analysis Method) * Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) * Quality Control Experience * Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) * Precision Measurement \& Inspection * Blueprint Reading **Ready to raise the bar? Let’s talk.**

jobs.title: Quantitative Researcher
jobs.description: **Who We Are** ============== **We’re on a mission to stop the most dominant cyberattacks on the planet.** Cybersecurity titans are born when a new attack vector overwhelms existing defenses. When ransomware ran rampant, CrowdStrike emerged as the category leader for securing user endpoints. Today, AI has made account compromise the \#1 cybercrime. LLM\-powered phishing messages get past email security, allowing attackers to compromise accounts and exfiltrate sensitive data in minutes. Incumbents can't keep up. They catch these attacks late, or miss them altogether. Enter Petra, security for when no perimeter remains. We are building an AI\-driven Detection and Response platform to catch and remove attackers before they can act. **We've grown very quickly,** reaching mid\-7\-figures in ARR in under a year and then doubling ARR in the past few months— we now protect over 2\.5 million users across 10,000\+ businesses. We price premium, yet have extremely low customer churn. Our customers consistently tell us that Petra is the best product they've ever used. You can see a demo here. **This is a rare chance to join early and help scale to $30M\+ in revenue in the next 12 months.** **What You’ll Do** ================== Ownership is everything here. You'll be responsible for our core ML detection research, and the models you design and deploy are what separate Petra from every other player in this space. Petra is a premium product and it's everyone's job to make sure it stays that way. That means you won't just train models — you'll talk to customers, understand the attacks they're facing, and think creatively about how to find the next signal that widens the gap between us and second place. Concretely, you will: * **Build and evolve our detection models.** Working closely with our CTO and Head of Machine Learning, you'll help design and build the ML models that identify account compromise in real time. * **Take models from research to production.** You don't just care about model performance in a notebook. You're energized by measuring how your models behave at scale in a live system with real attackers. * **Architect for scale.** We're growing fast. Nothing excites you more than architecting and implementing an elegant solution that'll handle 10\-100x the scale in 6 months. * **Develop and push the technical bar.** As a core voice on a lean team, your appetite and ability to learn quickly will be crucial to the teams experimentation and collective knowledge. You'll establish patterns, push for correctness, and raise the quality of everything around you. Our stack is Python, Node, TypeScript, and React... for now. **Who You Are** =============== * **1\-4 years of quantitative/machine learning research experience**, with meaningful time designing, training, evaluating, and shipping models in production systems at scale. * **Strong quantitative fundamentals:** probability \& statistics, linear algebra, linear and non\-linear modeling, NLP. * **Experience training \& deploying models in production:** You know how to pick the right model for the job. Just as importantly, you know the limitations of each modeling approach you consider. * **Strong engineering fundamentals** — you write clean, production\-grade code and are comfortable contributing to systems end to end, not just the modeling layer. * **Experience working with real\-time or streaming data pipelines, feature stores, high\-performance databases, and distributed systems**. Bonus if you've worked in high\-stakes domains like quantitative finance or fraud detection. * **High agency and high output**. You identify the problem, propose the solution, and execute. You're constantly looking for ways to expand your scope and circle of competence. * **Sharp and scrappy.** You learn fast: you ask the right questions and figure it out. You ship fast: you find the 90/10 and don't let perfect be the enemy of done. * **Comfortable in a small\-team, high\-autonomy environment**. The scope of your work is rarely handed to you, and you wouldn't have it any other way. * **Proud of your craft.** You care about building things that work well and hold up over time. **The Team** ============ We're small and high\-caliber. jobs.title: Senior Edge Engineer
jobs.description: **About Us** Queue builds robots to fill prescriptions. Our machine is designed to take stock bottles of medication and produce counted, labeled vials, so that pharmacists and technicians can spend their time on patients. Our first product is built to work behind the pharmacy counter and to be operated by pharmacy staff. **About the Role** We are building out the Edge squad: the engineers who write the software that runs on our machine and tells its hardware what to do. You own hard parts of that software end to end, from the links to the boards to the way a new version reaches a machine in the field and behaves there. On every path you own you build to one rule: when the machine cannot confirm a step, it stops safely and says why. This is a senior\-level role. **What You'll Own** * **Hardware links** — The edge software's side of the links to the motor board and the other controllers, over CAN, serial, USB and Ethernet: framing, timing, errors, reconnects and the tests that prove them. You set how they are built and tested. * **Fill sequencing** — The state machines that take a fill from the moment it reaches the machine to the moment the machine finishes or stops. You set how they are designed and tested. * **Contracts at the boundaries** — The contracts with the microcontrollers and the vision service. You version them and change them with the firmware and vision engineers, so that old and new versions work together through a release. * **What the software needs from the image** — The services, devices, bus settings and packages the edge software needs from the machine's Linux image. You make those changes with the engineers who own the image. * **Field behavior** — What the edge software reports from a machine in the field, how it is diagnosed from a distance, and its part in how a new version arrives and how it is rolled back if it fails. You build it with the platform and systems reliability engineers. * **Fail\-closed behavior** — The rule on every path you own: when the machine cannot confirm a step, it stops safely and says why. You design the failure path first and prove it on the bench. **First 90 Days** * **Day 30:** You have built the edge software, run it against the boards on a bench, and merged changes through review. You can trace a fill through the state machines and name each point where it has to stop if a step cannot be confirmed. * **Day 60:** You own a hardware link and its contract end to end. You have made a change to the machine's Linux image with the engineers who own it, and run it on a bench machine. * **Day 90:** You have taken a change from design through a release to a machine on the bench, with its failure paths tested first. You hold a written plan for what the edge software reports from the field and how it is diagnosed from a distance. **What We're Looking For** *Must\-Have* * Ownership — you have written production C, C\+\+ or Rust on Linux and owned what you shipped, from the first design to the fault found in the field. * Hardware integration over buses — CAN, RS\-485 and other serial links, USB. You have debugged a link with an analyzer on the wire when the logs and the hardware disagreed. * Real\-time orchestration and state machines — you have sequenced motion, sensing and I/O where partial failure is normal, and you design the failure path first: when a step cannot be confirmed, the system stops safely and says why. * MCU boundary literacy — you understand how a microcontroller runs and what it exposes to a Linux host, and you have kept versioned device protocols with firmware working through change, for example a protobuf schema, a CAN message set or a register map. * Embedded Linux integration — you have done substantial work getting software running well on an embedded Linux system: its services, devices, start\-up, configuration and updates, worked out with the owners of its image. * Connected device fleets — you have run devices in the field: updates, remote diagnostics, telemetry, and the recovery of a unit you cannot touch. The edge software is written in Rust, and you will work in it every day. Rust in production is preferred. *Nice\-to\-Have* * Industrial x86 and ARM platforms in a shipped product. * Full ownership of an embedded Linux distribution: building and maintaining the image of a shipped device, from what goes into it to how it updates. * Kernel and board bring\-up: drivers, device trees and boot on a new board. * Hardened device platforms: verified start\-up, signed updates, a read\-only system and device identity. * NVIDIA Jetson: JetPack and Linux for Tegra, secure boot, field updates and the inference stack. * Robotics, medical devices, automotive or industrial automation. **How We Hire** * **Recruiter Screen** (30 min) * **Technical Interview** (90 min) — a take\-home exercise of 2 to 3 hours, in C, C\+\+ or Rust, sent at least 24 hours before: a small piece of device software built around a state machine, which has to stay correct when power is lost at any step. We go through it together, then build on it. * **Design Interview** (60 min) — the path a new version of the software takes to a fleet of machines, with the failure cases in from the start. * **Leadership Interview** (60 min) — how you own your work and work across squads. Two interviewers score each technical stage independently. **What We Offer** * Ownership — hard parts of the edge software end to end, from the links to the boards to machines in the field * Hard problems: real\-time sequencing across boards, contracts with firmware and vision, and machines in the field you cannot touch * Small team, zero bureaucracy, high trust **Why Join Us Now?** *Impact \& Growth* * **Direct Impact:** The code you write tells the machine's hardware what to do, on the bench and in the field * **Growth:** The work runs from one hardware link to how the software behaves on every machine in the field *Team and Culture* * Reports to the Head of Software Engineering with significant autonomy and influence * **Who You Work With:** You work every day with the engineers who build the edge software, and closely with the firmware, vision, platform and systems reliability engineers * **Where We Work:** Hybrid, three days a week at our headquarters in the Bay Area; the bench work needs the hardware in front of you **Our Values** * **Servant Leadership** * **Do the Hard Things** * **Own Your Work** * **Default is Now** Own Your Work comes first in this role: what you ship to a machine is yours until it works there. **Contact: If you have any questions, please contact us at** **careers@queue.inc**

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Frontend Engineer
jobs.description: **About Us** Queue builds robots to fill prescriptions. Our machine is designed to take stock bottles of medication and produce counted, labeled vials, so that pharmacists and technicians can spend their time on patients. Our first product is built to work behind the pharmacy counter and to be operated by pharmacy staff. **About the Role** You own the screen that pharmacy staff will use to run the machine, and then every other screen Queue ships. The operator screen is a large, touch\-only panel on the front of the unit, built to be used all day by technicians who are busy with something else. You are answerable for three things: the screen that ships is the screen that was reviewed, a change in the design reaches the machine in days, and the next screen is built to the frontend standard you keep. This posting covers Senior and Staff levels. Senior level means you own this surface end to end. Staff level means the frontend standard and review practice carry your name, and other engineers build against them. The technical interview is set at the Senior bar. **What You'll Own** * **The operator screen** — Its scope is the prescription queue, replenishment of drugs and consumables, machine health, administration and exception handling, and sign\-in on an on\-screen keypad. * **The prototype and the application** — The interface has two forms: the design prototype that is reviewed, and the React application for the machine. You are answerable for the match between them, working with our product designer. * **The rules of touch** — There is no mouse and no keyboard. Touch targets are never smaller than 48 pixels. Text can be read at a glance in the middle of another task. The screen advances on physical events, such as a drawer closing, and not on extra taps. An action that cannot be undone is never placed where fast fingers land. * **What interrupts a technician** — A model with three layers: ambient status, a call for attention, and a blocking dialog, with clear rules for which is used when. That includes the alerts for the machine's own faults. * **Working in the interface contract** — The screen owns no domain state: it renders what the machine sends, so a reload always lands on the truth. Its TypeScript types are generated from the Rust source on the machine, and the build fails when they drift. The engineers who own the on\-machine software own the contract; you work in it with them every day. * **The quality bar** — You set it and hold every screen to it: unit tests with coverage measured, end\-to\-end tests in a real browser, and lint rules that enforce the design tokens. * **The screens that follow** — Our cloud operations dashboard comes next, and then the screens of later products. They are built to the standard you set on the operator screen, on smaller displays as well as large ones. **First 90 Days** * **Day 30:** You have merged a change to the screen. You know the queue, replenishment and alert flows as a technician will meet them, you have sat in a design review, and you have gone through the prototype and the application side by side with our product designer. * **Day 60:** Design changes reach the application through your own commits. The three\-layer interruption model is yours, alerts included. Your end\-to\-end suite runs the flows a technician will run every day. * **Day 90:** You are answerable for the match between the application and the reviewed design, and for the screen's readiness for security review. You keep the frontend standard: testing, tokens, review, and how screens work within the contract. You have a dated plan for the next screen, the cloud operations dashboard. **What We're Looking For** *Must\-Have* * Ownership — you have owned a product surface that people depended on every day, from the first design conversation to the fault found in the field, and you can show what you changed after it went wrong. * Strict TypeScript — the strictest compiler settings are where you are at home, and you write types that make an invalid state impossible to express. * React 19 with the React Compiler — your components follow the Rules of React because they have to. * State discipline — you have built over state the server owns, delivered by WebSocket, and you understand why a screen that owns no domain state is safer. * Our tools — Tailwind 4, Vite, Vitest and Playwright, with component tests and real\-browser tests as a habit. * Work with design — you have turned a designer's living prototype into production software without losing the intent, and you can disagree with a designer and still ship. *Important* Working knowledge is enough, and we teach the rest. * Touch interfaces on fixed devices — large targets, keypads drawn by the application, protection against a mis\-tap. * Explicit states — you reason in states and transitions, which is how the whole system is built. We do not ask for Rust. The types are generated for you. *Nice\-to\-Have* * Accessibility in depth, including WCAG 2\.1 AA, and responsive web work. * Interfaces for embedded browsers, point\-of\-sale or other constrained devices. * Healthcare or another regulated industry. * A design system or standard that other engineers adopted. **How We Hire** * **Recruiter Screen** (30 min) * **Technical Interview** (90 min) — a walk through your take\-home exercise of 2 to 3 hours, sent at least 24 hours before, then we build on it together. * **Design Interview** (60 min) — an interaction and architecture problem that changes as we go. * **Leadership Interview** (60 min) — how you own your work and work across squads. Two interviewers score each technical stage independently. At Staff level, the Design Interview also looks for more than one option weighed, with the trade\-offs written down, and for how other engineers would review the design and take it up. The Leadership Interview also looks for how you have raised a standard across teams: a practice you rolled out that stuck, engineers you helped lead, and disagreement worked through. **What We Offer** * Ownership — the operator screen end to end, then every screen that follows * Hard problems: touch\-only interaction, interruptions a busy technician can act on, and a typed contract with the software on the machine * Small team, zero bureaucracy, high trust **Why Join Us Now?** *Impact \& Growth* * **Direct Impact:** The screen you build is the one pharmacy staff will use to run the machine * **Growth:** The standard you set on this screen is the one every later screen is built to *Team and Culture* * Reports to the Head of Software Engineering with significant autonomy and influence * **Who You Work With:** You work every day with our product designer and with the engineers who own the on\-machine software * **Where We Work:** Hybrid, three days a week at our headquarters in the Bay Area; the screen you build is bolted to a machine **Our Values** * **Servant Leadership** * **Do the Hard Things** * **Own Your Work** * **Default is Now** Own Your Work comes first in this role: a mis\-tap on this screen is your problem before it is anyone else's. **Contact: If you have any questions, please contact us at** **careers@queue.inc**

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Frontend
jobs.description: **LUZID** **Software Engineer, Frontend** San Francisco, in\-person 4x/week **About Luzid** Luzid is building the operating system for SAP delivery — the infrastructure layer underneath the most complex and expensive IT projects companies run. SAP implementations move billions of dollars and thousands of consultants, but the knowledge generated in these projects is never captured: it lives in people's heads, disappears when the project ends, and gets rebuilt from scratch on every new engagement. Luzid solves this with an agentic orchestration platform that coordinates every phase of SAP transformation, capturing decisions, tests, and context as a byproduct of work already underway — building an organizational memory that accumulates across projects instead of resetting. We're a team based in San Francisco and São Paulo, moving fast and already deployed with some of the largest SAP integrators in the world, including delaware Consulting, KPMG, and NTT Data. We have reached \>$3M ARR in 11 months and raised $21M in funding. The team comes from Stanford, Meta, Two Sigma, Microsoft, and NASA. **The Opportunity** You'll build the interfaces consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents. These workflows involve substantial information, interconnected decisions, and work that unfolds over time. Your job is to make that complexity understandable and manageable through thoughtful, responsive software. You'll work closely with design and other engineers, and talk directly to customers to understand where they're encountering friction. You'll help shape what we build, prototype alternatives, ship improvements, and follow through on how they perform in production. Your primary focus will be the frontend: both the experiences users interact with and the foundations that help our team build them well. You'll have room to make consequential technical decisions and the responsibility to keep them practical — using AI\-assisted development tools to explore and iterate, while applying your own judgment to the quality and simplicity of what we ship. **What You'll Do** * **Own product outcomes.** Take ambiguous problems from customer conversations through implementation, deployment, and iteration. * **Build the core interfaces.** Ship the experiences consultants and enterprise teams use to navigate complex implementations and work with AI agents. * **Reason from UX back into implementation.** Decide which interactions need to feel instantaneous, how state and data should flow, and when a problem calls for a better component, a different loading strategy, or a change to an API. * **Design for real usage.** Think through loading, empty, error, and recovery states; collaborate closely with design; treat accessibility as part of a complete experience. * **Build durable foundations.** Recognize reusable interaction patterns, design clear component APIs, and use composition and shared primitives to keep the product consistent as it grows. * **Make the product feel fast.** Reason about rendering, network requests, caching, prefetching, and feedback during longer operations — and measure whether changes actually help. * **Work across boundaries.** Reason about APIs, data models, and backend behavior when they affect the frontend, and make pragmatic build\-vs\-use calls. * **Raise the team's bar.** Work independently, communicate decisions clearly, and improve the experience of engineers building alongside you — including how the team uses AI\-assisted workflows. **What We're Looking For** * **Deep frontend fundamentals.** You've shipped and maintained complex interactive applications, and understand JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML and CSS, browser behavior, rendering, state management, and asynchronous data flow. * **Strong UX judgment.** You think in terms of how people will actually use a feature, not just whether it works. * **Evidence\-driven.** You combine customer feedback with analytics, performance monitoring, and session replay to identify friction and evaluate the impact of changes. * **Ownership.** You ask questions, challenge assumptions, and care whether what you shipped actually helped, not just whether it shipped. * **Pragmatism.** You know when to use an existing library, when custom implementation is worthwhile, and how to balance immediate delivery with longer\-term maintainability. * **Curiosity and judgment.** Above all, you understand problems deeply, explore possible solutions, and make thoughtful trade\-offs between user experience, engineering quality, speed, and complexity. **Nice to have** * Experience building jobs.title: Staff/Senior Quantitative Researcher
jobs.description: **Who We Are** ============== **We’re on a mission to stop the most dominant cyberattacks on the planet.** Cybersecurity titans are born when a new attack vector overwhelms existing defenses. When ransomware ran rampant, CrowdStrike emerged as the category leader for securing user endpoints. Today, AI has made account compromise the \#1 cybercrime. LLM\-powered phishing messages get past email security, allowing attackers to compromise accounts and exfiltrate sensitive data in minutes. Incumbents can't keep up. They catch these attacks late, or miss them altogether. Enter Petra, security for when no perimeter remains. We are building an AI\-driven Detection and Response platform to catch and remove attackers before they can act. **We've grown very quickly,** reaching mid\-7\-figures in ARR in under a year and then doubling ARR in the past few months— we now protect over 2\.5 million users across 10,000\+ businesses. We price premium, yet have extremely low customer churn. Our customers consistently tell us that Petra is the best product they've ever used. You can see a demo here. **This is a rare chance to join early and help scale to $30M\+ in revenue in the next 12 months.** **What You’ll Do** ================== Ownership is everything here. You'll be responsible for our core ML detection research, and the models you design and deploy are what separate Petra from every other player in this space. Petra is a premium product and it's everyone's job to make sure it stays that way. That means you won't just train models — you'll talk to customers, understand the attacks they're facing, and think creatively about how to find the next signal that widens the gap between us and second place. Concretely, you will: * **Build and evolve our detection models.** Working closely with our CTO and Head of Machine Learning, you'll design and build the ML models that identify account compromise in real time. * **Take models from research to production.** You don't just care about model performance in a notebook. You're energized by measuring how your models behave at scale in a live system with real attackers. * **Architect for scale.** We're growing fast. Nothing excites you more than architecting and implementing an elegant solution that'll handle 10\-100x the scale in 6 months. * **Raise the technical bar.** As a senior voice on a lean team, your instincts and opinions shape how we build. You'll establish patterns, push for correctness, and raise the quality of everything around you. Our stack is Python, Node, TypeScript, and React... for now. **Who You Are** =============== * **5\+ years of quantitative/machine learning research experience**, with meaningful time designing, training, evaluating, and shipping models in production systems at scale. * **Strong quantitative fundamentals:** probability \& statistics, linear algebra, linear and non\-linear modeling, NLP. * **Experience training \& deploying models in production:** You know how to pick the right model for the job. Just as importantly, you know the limitations of each modeling approach you consider. * **Strong engineering fundamentals** — you write clean, production\-grade code and are comfortable owning a system end to end, not just the modeling layer. * **Experience working with real\-time or streaming data pipelines, feature stores, high\-performance databases, and distributed systems**. Bonus if you've worked in high\-stakes domains like quantitative finance or fraud detection. * **High agency and high output**. You identify the problem, propose the solution, and execute. You're constantly looking for ways to expand your scope and circle of competence. * **Sharp and scrappy.** You learn fast: you ask the right questions and figure it out. You ship fast: you find the 90/10 and don't let perfect be the enemy of done. * **Comfortable in a small\-team, high\-autonomy environment**. The scope of your work is rarely handed to you, and you wouldn't have it any other way. * **Proud of your craft.** You care about building things that work well and hold up over time. **The Team** ============ We're small and high\-caliber. Our founders are ex\-Abnormal Security, Palo Alto Networks, and Bridgewater. Other early team members include: * A Sequoia\-backed founder * An engineering leader from Anduril * Quant researchers and engineers from IMC, SIG, Citadel, and Cubist You'll work directly with people who are exceptional at what they do. **Benefits and Pay:** ===================== * Competitive salary. We pay top dollar for exceptional researchers. * Equity * Healthcare, dental, vision * Lunch and dinner when working in the office * 401K * Commuting stipend * Equinox discount * Relocation support This role is in\-person, here in SF. \- *Petra is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team and welcome applicants of all backgrounds.*

jobs.description: **Our Mission** --------------- Our mission is to restore cell health and resilience through cell rejuvenation to reverse disease, injury, and the disabilities that can occur throughout life. Our intentional focus is on Belonging, so that all employees know that they are valued for their unique perspectives. We are all accountable for sustaining a diverse and inclusive environment. **What You Will Contribute To Altos** ------------------------------------- * As a contract Senior Knowledge Engineer, Ontology and Data Standards, you will drive how our team represents biological knowledge At Altos * We have built the machinery: a large canonical LinkML/Biolink schema including REST/MCP/CLI service layer; specification packages covering multiple prior\-knowledge sources; and an agentic / human\-in\-the\-loop curation framework. What it lacks is a technical owner—someone to govern and administer the content. * You are the scientific translation layer between biological discovery and AI platform engineering. You will elicit implicit models from bench and computational scientists, encode them rigorously, and utilize the agentic workflows that scale curation beyond what manual review can reach. * This role carries explicit decision rights: review authority on canonical schema change, ownership of the curation conventions that data atlas and engineering teams follow. **Key Responsibilities** * Knowledge Modeling \& Ontology Engineering: + Design, maintain, and extend internal LinkML / Biolink models and ontologies covering experimental and prior\-knowledge metadata—driven by competency questions from user requirements and not by source\-side convenience. + Own mapping and alignment as a discipline: cross\-ontology mappings with recorded justification and provenance, and upstream term requests as appropriate. + Serve as reviewer of record for schema change, holding the line that reuse precedes coining anything new. * Agentic \& Automated Curation: + Administer, steer, and refine our agentic curation framework and Model Context Protocol (MCP) service layer to scale data profiling, validation, and entity mapping far beyond manual capacity. + Standardize tool definitions (FastMCP), prompt templates, and LLM\-driven workflows that extract, normalize, and validate metadata from prior\-knowledge sources and experimental assets. * Biological Data Harmonization: + Define mapping patterns and metadata conventions for diverse experimental modalities (genomics, single\-cell, screening data) to conform to the canonical schema. + Establish standardized conventions that allow both external prior\-knowledge sources and internal experimental datasets to cleanly map into the LinkML graph architecture. * Quality, Evaluation \& Provenance: + Establish and maintain automated validation, LLM\-assisted quality control, and CI/CD under a "curation as code" paradigm—extending existing drift and coverage gates into the places where semantic review is still manual. + Measure whether the knowledge is correct, not merely reproducible: gold\-standard sets, inter\-curator agreement, and precision/recall on automated extraction. **Who You Are** --------------- * Education \& Experience: This is a senior individual\-contributor role with organization\-wide technical authority and no direct reports. * Biological Data Lifecycle: Direct experience turning messy, real\-world exploratory datasets (genomics, single\-cell, screening, imaging) into structured metadata. * Ontology \& Semantic Web Expertise: Strong working knowledge of OBO Foundry standards, OWL, RDF, and SPARQL, with schema modeling experience in LinkML, Biolink, or BioCypher. Experience with Protégé, ROBOT, ODK, or SSSOM mapping sets is a plus. * Python \& Agentic AI Tooling: Proficient in modular Python (3\.12, uv, pandas, Pydantic, pytest), and able to read and extend a substantial existing codebase rather than only scripting against it. Active hands\-on experience with AI environments (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code) and building agentic LLM workflows, custom MCP tools, or RAG pipelines. * Software \& Data Management: Familiarity with Git, GitHub Actions, graph/relational databases, and cloud storage (e.g., AWS S3\). jobs.description: **DESCRIPTION** --------------- Do you want to be part of AI revolution? At Amazon our vision is to make deep learning pervasive for everyday developers and to democratize access to AI hardware and software infrastructure. In order to deliver on that vision, we’ve created innovative software and hardware solutions that make it possible. AWS Neuron is the SDK that optimizes the performance of complex ML models executed on AWS Inferentia and Trainium, our custom chips designed to accelerate deep\-learning workloads. This role is for a software engineer in the Compiler team for AWS Neuron. As part of this role, you will be responsible for building next generation Neuron compiler which transforms ML models written in ML frameworks (e.g, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX) to be deployed AWS Inferentia and Trainium based servers in the Amazon cloud. You will be responsible for solving hard compiler optimization problems to achieve optimum performance for variety of ML model families including massive scale large language models like Llama, Deepseek, and beyond as well as stable diffusion, vision transformers and multi\-model models. You will be required to understand how these models work inside\-out to make informed decisions on how to best coax the compiler to generate optimal implementation instruction. You will leverage your technical communications skill to partner with internal and external customers/stakeholders and will be involved in pre\-silicon design, bringing new products/features to market, ultimately, making Neuron compiler highly performant and easy\-to\-use. Experience in object\-oriented languages like C\+\+/Java is a must, experience with compilers or building ML models using ML frameworks on accelerators (e.g., GPUs) is preferred but not required. Experience with technologies like OpenXLA, StableHLO, MLIR will be added bonus! jobs.title: Sr. Software Dev Engineer, AWS Insights and Optimizations
jobs.description: **DESCRIPTION** --------------- Every AWS customer wants to know the same thing: am I paying for more cloud than I actually need? AWS Insights and Optimizations is the team that answers that question, for millions of accounts, across compute, storage, databases, and commitment purchases. We analyze resource insights, compute recommendations against the latest AWS offerings and pricing models, and build the tooling that automates the optimization workflow end to end. That question has gotten harder and more expensive to get wrong. AI and machine learning workloads are now the fastest growing line on many customers' bills. Accelerated compute is scarce and costly, training and inference usage is bursty and hard to forecast, and the usual rules of thumb for whether a resource is right\-sized do not transfer cleanly to a GPU fleet or an inference endpoint. Customers want the same clarity on their AI spend that they have come to expect on the rest of their infrastructure, and today most of them do not have it. Closing that gap is a significant part of where this team is going. You would own the foundation the whole experience is delivered on. Customers come at optimization from a lot of directions: the console, our public APIs, a partner product, an export into their own reporting stack, a conversation with their support team, or an agent asking on their behalf. Every one of those paths runs through the platform in this role, so the work is a customer experience problem before it is an infrastructure problem. A finance lead needs to see an entire organization at once rather than one account at a time. An engineer deciding whether to accept a change needs the answer quickly, needs it to reflect this week's usage and not last quarter's, and needs to understand how we reached it before they will act on it. A partner or a customer's own automation needs to build on us and still work a year from now. Who we serve is also changing. The experience was designed for a person clicking through a console, and it is increasingly driven by agents that run continuously, ask in bulk, and need to know not only what we recommend but why. We treat that as a build mandate rather than a buzzword. You would help redesign the optimization experience around generative AI: opening the platform to agents through MCP and agent\-friendly contracts, carrying enough provenance with every recommendation that an agent can justify an action to the human accountable for it, supporting multi\-step and batch work instead of one question at a time, modernizing authentication for machine\-to\-machine scale, and making the system behave under continuous, bursty, non\-human load. You would use the same tools on your own work. Agents are already part of how this team builds and operates, and we would want you pushing that further. If you like owning a broadly used API surface, care about the difference between a recommendation that is technically correct and one that earns a customer's trust, and want your work to show up as real dollars off real bills, come talk to us. Key job responsibilities * Own the public API surface customers, partners, and other AWS services depend on to enroll, retrieve recommendations, export data, and express how they want their environment optimized, including the cross\-account and organization\-wide access model behind it. * Design for agents as first\-class consumers: programmatic and MCP access, bulk and multi\-step operations, machine\-to\-machine authentication, and capacity and throttling behavior that holds up under continuous automated load. * Extend the platform to AI and accelerated compute spend, including the question of what optimal even means for workloads whose usage patterns look nothing like a traditional server fleet. * Make recommendations explainable and self\-diagnosable, so that customers and support teams can answer why a recommendation says what it says, or why it is missing, without an engineer in the loop. * Raise the operational bar: how we monitor, test, deploy, and expand across Regions and partitions, and how much of the recurring operational load we can automate away instead of absorbing. * Grow the engineers around you. Review designs, mentor, and write the documents that build consensus with stakeholders across organizations. * Work directly with product managers and with the teams building on your APIs to decide what to build, proactively identify what is blocking the team and what the platform will need as usage grows, before either becomes a constraint. A day in the life You might spend the morning in a design review arguing whether a new capability belongs in the public API, then pair with an engineer on failure handling in a cross\-account delivery path, then dig into a signal that says customers are enrolling but encountering issues in the optimization journey, then point an agent at your own API to find out how badly it reads to a non\-human caller. Some weeks are heads\-down implementation. Some weeks are writing the document that decides the next six months. About the team AWS Insights and Optimizations is a group of engineers who like problems that sit between large\-scale data processing and customer\-facing APIs, and we are unusually close to the outcome of our work, because we can measure it in savings customers actually realized. We are among the more fastest\-moving adopters of generative AI in AWS cloud financial management, in the product and in how we build and operate it. We care about operational excellence, we write things down, and we would rather have the hard architectural conversation early than live with the shortcut for three years. The charter is expanding and there is real room to shape it.**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS** ------------------------ * 5\+ years of non\-internship professional software development experience * 5\+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience * 5\+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience * Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** ---------------------------- * 5\+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience * Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent * Experience building and operating public, customer\-facing APIs, including versioning and backward compatibility over a long service life * Experience with multi\-tenant systems and the authorization, isolation, and quota problems that come with them * Experience building agent\-facing or LLM\-integrated systems, for example MCP servers, tool and function interfaces, or retrieval over structured data * Experience with large\-scale data processing, indexing, or search systems behind a customer\-facing product Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.
